title: Atlanta’s lead grows—but one point comes back.
summary: Across the visible score graphics, Atlanta moves from 56 to 67 while Milwaukee stays at 51. The displayed lead grows from 5 to 16. But Atlanta briefly shows 62 before dropping to 61: adding only the upward changes would overcount by one point.
provenance: Prepared by Codex from 71 locally decoded source frames, sampled roughly once per second across this 70.2-second clip. This is an editorial source review, not a new result from the app’s Gemini pipeline.

insight.title: The easy-to-miss detail: 62 → 61
insight.observation: The broadcast graphic reads Atlanta 62 at 00:36.036 and 61 at 00:37.037. Milwaukee remains at 51.
insight.interpretation: A downward display revision changes the total. The footage alone does not establish whether this was an official scoring correction or a broadcast graphic error.

chapters.title: Opening possession and a larger lead
chapters.text: The opening wide shot shows Atlanta in white attacking the left basket. The display changes from 56–51 to 59–51, followed by a player close-up. Replay the possession to inspect the movement leading to the change.

chapters.title: Opposite-end play, then another Atlanta increase
chapters.text: The broadcast returns to the right basket, follows players back toward the left, then shows 62–51 and cuts to the crowd. The game clock jumps across the edit; these shots do not establish every intervening possession.

chapters.title: Transition and a downward score revision
chapters.text: Court action moves from the right end toward the left. As Atlanta advances, its displayed score changes from 62 to 61. The reason is not visible in these sampled frames.

chapters.title: The display reaches 64; reaction shots follow
chapters.text: A wide Atlanta attacking sequence is followed by a crowd shot showing 64–51, then player and bench close-ups. These reaction shots interrupt the view of play; they are not additional scoring events.

chapters.title: Another end-to-end sequence and 67–51
chapters.text: The broadcast returns to Milwaukee’s attacking end, follows play toward Atlanta’s basket, and then displays 67–51. The cited frames support the score change; player attribution and tactical cause need closer replay.

chapters.title: Players, bench and crowd close the clip
chapters.text: The ending consists of close-ups and reactions. It does not show the end of the game, so this excerpt cannot establish the final result or what happened next.
